name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER9_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Chronological steps of MOET in cattle

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps of Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET) in cattle in the correct chronological sequence:

  • P. Non-surgical recovery of fertilised eggs at 8–32 cell stages
  • Q. Administration of hormones with FSH-like activity to induce follicular maturation and superovulation
  • R. Transfer of recovered embryos to surrogate mothers
  • S. Mating the cow with an elite bull or carrying out artificial insemination

Choose the correct sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET) is a controlled breeding programme designed to improve herd quality and increase herd size rapidly.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Sequencing
1. First, a cow is administered hormones with FSH-like activity to induce follicular maturation and superovulation, producing 6 to 8 eggs per cycle instead of the normal single egg.
2. Second, the superovulated animal is either mated with an elite bull or artificially inseminated.
3. Third, the fertilised eggs at the 8 to 32 cell stages are recovered non-surgically from the genetic mother.
4. Fourth, the recovered embryos are transferred to surrogate mothers, leaving the genetic mother available for another round of superovulation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is: hormone administration for superovulation → mating or artificial insemination → non-surgical recovery of 8–32 cell stage fertilised eggs → transfer to surrogate mothers.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER9_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequential steps of somatic hybridisation in plants

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps involved in producing a somatic hybrid plant in vitro in the correct logical sequence:

  • P. Fusion of isolated protoplasts from two different plant varieties to obtain hybrid protoplasts
  • Q. Isolation of single cells from plants of two different varieties having desirable characters
  • R. Growth of hybrid protoplasts in culture to regenerate a new somatic hybrid plant
  • S. Digestion of cell walls to isolate naked protoplasts surrounded by plasma membranes

Choose the correct sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Somatic hybridisation enables the combination of desirable traits from two different plant varieties by fusing their somatic protoplasts rather than sexual gametes.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Sequencing
1. First, single cells are isolated from plants of two different varieties, each possessing a desirable character.
2. Second, the cell walls of these isolated cells are digested to obtain naked protoplasts surrounded only by plasma membranes.
3. Third, the isolated naked protoplasts from the two varieties are fused to form hybrid protoplasts.
4. Fourth, the hybrid protoplasts are cultured further in vitro to grow into a new somatic hybrid plant.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is: isolation of single cells → digestion of cell walls to obtain naked protoplasts → fusion of protoplasts to form hybrid protoplasts → growth of hybrid protoplasts into a somatic hybrid plant.
